annotations.title: Auarice, vvhich is the ſeruice of idols.
annotations.text: ◦ Here is a maruelous impudent and foliſh corruption in the vulgar Engliſh Bible printed the yere 1577 and (as it ſeemeth) moſt authoriſed. Vvhere for their errour againſt the Images of Chriſt and his Saincts, and to make image and idol, al one: the tranſlator, for that vvhich the Apoſtle ſaith in Greeke, Couetouſnes is idolatrie, maketh him to ſay in Engliſh, Couetouſnes is vvorſhipping of images: as alſo Eph. 5, 4 he tranſlateth thus, The couetous perſon is a vvorſhipper of images: for that vvhich the Apoſtle ſaith, The couetous man is an idolater, meaning ſpiritual idolatrie, becauſe he maketh money his God. In vvhich ſenſe to call this ſpiritual idolatrie, vvorſhipping of images, is to ridiculous, and muſt needes procede of blinde hereſie.

annotations.title: Doing on the new.
annotations.text: ◦ By this and the whole diſcourſe of this chapter containing an exhortation to good life, and to put on the habit of the new man vvith all virtues: vve may ſee, our iuſtice in Chriſt to be a very qualitie and form inherent in our ſoul, adorning the ſame, and not an imputation only of Chriſt's righteouſnes, or a hiding only of our ſins and vvickednes, which the Heretics falſely affirme to remaine in vs after baptiſm and always during life. See S. Auguſtine de pec. mer. & remiſ. li. 2. c. 7. & cont. Iulian. li. 6. c. 7.

notes.text: Justice an inherent quality in us.
